question: Should OpenClaw adopt this Discord subagent-progress feature with the proposed generic channel lifecycle callback, delivery-context field, persisted cleanup marker, and seven configuration settings?
rationale: The implementation is technically coherent and well proven, but repository policy sets a high bar for new configuration and plugin API surfaces; deciding whether these contracts should become permanent requires owner intent rather than automated repair.

options.title: Sponsor the proposed contracts
options.body: Approve the default-off feature and additive contracts, then require a conflict-resolved refresh and exact-head validation before merge.

options.title: Request a narrower internal seam
options.body: Keep the Discord UX but redesign completion cleanup to avoid or reduce new published lifecycle and configuration surface.

options.title: Decline the product surface
options.body: Close the PR if configurable source-message progress is not a core Discord capability OpenClaw wants to maintain.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the proposed contracts
recommendation.body: Approve the default-off feature and additive contracts, then require a conflict-resolved refresh and exact-head validation before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice centers on plugin hook and agent lifecycle architecture rather than a mechanical Discord repair.
